title: Queue shepherding: adaptive micro-batch thresholds and backpressure for sustained high QPS
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Under prolonged high QPS (5k-15k reqs/s per cluster) we observe repeated tail-latency spikes and intermittent GPU memory pressure that lead to soft failures and elevated token cost. Existing admission controllers use static micro-batch ceilings and coarse KV eviction signals which either over-throttle (wasting capacity) or under-react (OOMs and poor tails).

Goal: Design and ship an adaptive "queue shepherding" controller that dynamically adjusts micro-batch admission thresholds and soft backpressure signals based on short-horizon QPS forecasts, KV cache hotness heatmap, and GPU slab pressure. The controller should preserve p50 latency and SLOs while reducing p95/p99 tail and the frequency of KV-induced OOM/eviction cascades. It should integrate with the existing admission API and expose diagnostics to Console and logging.

Scope: algorithm design, runtime integration, a small stateful predictor, KV compaction hinting, conservative GPU headroom estimator, in-cluster A/B canary, dashboards, and docs. Not in scope: new kernel changes, model architecture changes, or customer-facing API surface changes.
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency reduced by >=12% under sustained 10k QPS workload compared to baseline (controlled experiment)
KV eviction storms frequency reduced by >=30% during the same workload window
No regression (>3%) on p50 latency for typical PLG workloads
Controller exposes per-tenant headroom, admitted-batch-size, and rejection-reason fields to Console and logs
End-to-end integration test that simulates QPS ramp and validates admission behavior under synthetic KV-hot keys
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with serving, infra, and observability. Agreed on three signals: short-horizon QPS delta (1-10s), KV hotness ratio (hot keys fraction in top-N), and GPU vacancy percent (slab level).
2026-03-04: PoC of short-horizon predictor delivered (Miguel). Uses exponential smoothing + seasonal damp to predict 5s QPS delta. Lightweight (single-threaded) to avoid CPU pressure.
2026-03-06: Design review feedback from Priya (SRE): require graceful degrade path that prefers per-tenant soft-reject over global throttles. Also asked to add telemetry for CPU cost of controller.

2026-03-08: Implemented KV compaction hint API: controller can emit a 'compact-hint' tag for tenants predicted to provoke high eviction. This allows KV service to pre-compact in background. (PR linked below)

2026-03-10: Canary started in eu-west-1 on a small fleet (10% capacity). Early results show fewer eviction spikes but slight increase in scheduler CPU. Monitoring flagged a few cold-start misses — added minor code change to prioritize first-token latency.
2026-03-11: UX review: Console team requested clearer labeling for 'headroom' and suggested adding historical slider for debugging regressions. Accepted and added to scope.

2026-03-12: Code review comments from runtime team: simplify admission state machine and add unit tests for edge race where KV hotness counter resets during eviction. Miguel addressing comments in next PR iteration.
experiment_results: Canary (eu-west-1, 10% traffic): 10-minute sustained 10k QPS synthetic test => baseline p95=420ms, shepherding p95=361ms (14% improvement)
KV eviction storm events per hour during stress window: baseline=3.7, shepherding=1.9 (49% reduction) due to earlier compaction hints and reduced oversubscription
GPU slab pressure OOM signals: baseline saw 6 OOM-like recoveries in 24h test; shepherding saw 1 recovery (83% fewer recoveries)
Token throughput cost: measured 22% lower effective token cost at 10k QPS in canary because of higher micro-batch utilization without tail latency regressions
CPU overhead: controller + predictor added ~6% CPU utilization on the serving control plane; within SRE acceptable limit but requires a tuned JVM flag on small instances
decisions: Use short-horizon exponential smoother for QPS forecast instead of heavy ML predictor to keep overhead low
Expose only soft-rejects and per-tenant advisories in first iteration; block/kill actions deferred to next cycle
KV compaction will be executed as a best-effort background job in KV service after receiving 'compact-hint' to avoid synchronous stalls
Admission state persisted in lightweight in-memory ringbuffer (no new external DB) to minimize latency; we will snapshot metrics to long-term stores for diagnostics
next_steps: Address runtime PR review comments and add the unit tests for KV counter race (Miguel) - due 2026-03-14
Complete Console labels and historical slider (Design) - due 2026-03-16
Run a 48h canary with mixed real traffic in us-west-2 and measure p99 and PLG regressions - schedule for 2026-03-17
If canary passes, prepare rollout playbook and feature flag gating for runtime-2.3 release window
